title: Careful Hugs
summary: Espín has the biggest heart in the forest and would love to hug his friends. But every time he tries, his spines stand on end.

scenes.text:
At the edge of the forest, where the meadow begins, lived a little hedgehog called Espín.

Espín had the biggest heart in the whole forest. And he had three friends: Coni the rabbit; Fito the fox; and Lino the badger, who was old and grumpy but very kind underneath.

Coni, Fito and Lino hugged each other all the time. To say hello. To say goodbye. To celebrate finding blackberries.

Espín watched them and longed to join in.

But Espín was a hedgehog. And hedgehogs have spines.

Especially when they get excited. Then their spines stand on end, all at once, like a cross hairbrush.

One afternoon, Coni won the race to the big tree.

"I won! I won!" she shouted, bouncing up and down.

Espín was so happy for her that he couldn't help himself. He ran at her with his arms wide open, threw himself into a hug and…

"OUCH!"

Coni gave such a leap that she ended up dangling from a branch.

"Sorry, sorry, sorry," said Espín.

He tried again with Fito, more slowly. But he got excited halfway there, his spines stood on end, and Fito went away with a tail full of tiny holes.

Espín looked at his spines. He felt like crying.

At sunset, Espín sat on a stone all by himself.

He had found a red leaf shaped like a heart, and he was holding it in his paws, not quite sure what for.

Lino the badger came along slowly, grumbling, and sat down beside him.

"What's the matter, little pincushion?"

"I want to give hugs," said Espín. "But I always prickle."

Lino looked at him for a long time.

"Have you noticed when your spines stand up?" he asked. "When you're running. When you get very excited. When your heart is racing."

"So?"

"So try it slowly."

The next day, Espín went to find Coni, with the red leaf in his paw.

This time he didn't run. He walked slowly. Very slowly.

Before he got there, he stopped. He closed his eyes and breathed.

In… and out. In… and out.

His heart calmed down, like a swing coming to a stop. And little by little, without him doing anything, his spines lay down, soft, like grass when the wind blows over it.

Espín gave Coni the red leaf. And very, very carefully, he hugged her.

Coni stayed very still. Then she began to giggle.

"It doesn't prickle at all! It's the softest hug in the world!"

Ever since that day, Espín gives careful hugs.

He comes close slowly. He breathes. He waits for his spines to lie down. And then he hugs.

His hugs take a little longer than everybody else's. But Fito says that's why they're the best: because they last longer.

That night, the four of them stayed in the meadow watching the moon come up, as thin as a fingernail.

Coni snuggled up on one side of Espín. Fito, on the other. And Lino, grumbling, settled down behind.

And like that, squeezed together and cosy, they fell asleep. Lino was the first: in no time at all, he was snoring.
